conventions.convention: Support is the set of points with nonzero germ, without taking an additional closure. For sheaves it is closed in the section's domain. Compact support means intrinsic compactness of this set.

C-softness means surjectivity of global sections onto sections of the inverse-image sheaf on every compact subset of a locally compact Hausdorff space. The definition places no support restriction on the global extension.
Compactly supported cohomology is computed using the supplied functorial injective resolution datum on abelian sheaves under AC; H_c^q is zero for q < 0. On compact spaces Γ_c = Γ and H_c^q = H^q.
The compatible-refinement assertion covers all tuples, including repeated indices; empty intersections require no covering witness. The original index set and resulting refinement are finite.
The Čech comparison concerns the refinement limit over all open covers of a compact Hausdorff space, equivalently finite covers, rather than an arbitrary fixed cover.

Cover order at most d + 1 means that each point belongs to at most d + 1 members. The resulting vanishing bound applies to arbitrary abelian sheaves and compactly supported cohomology on every open subspace.

The fibre-dimension hypothesis is uniform over every open subspace of every fibre and every coefficient sheaf. The conclusion is a length-d resolution of a sheaf, including the identity resolution when d = 0; it does not assert a compatible resolution of bounded complexes.

load_bearing.statement: Under AC on a locally compact Hausdorff space, c-soft abelian sheaves admit compactly supported extensions with prescribed neighbourhood support and have H_c^q = 0 for q > 0; injective abelian sheaves are c-soft. C-softness survives open and closed restriction, open extension by zero and finite sums, and constant-vector tensor products in the field case. A short exact sequence with c-soft kernel is exact on Γ_c and admits local lifts over compact sets; a c-soft kernel and middle term give a c-soft quotient.

For a compact subset K of a locally compact Hausdorff space and an abelian sheaf F, the canonical map colim_{U ⊇ K, U open} F(U) → Γ(K,i⁻¹F) is an isomorphism. Sections prescribed near finitely many pairwise disjoint compact subsets can be realized by one section near their union. No choice principle is used.

Under AC, Γ_c(X,F) consists of global sections with compact support and is an additive left exact functor on abelian sheaves; H_c^q is its right derived functor computed from the supplied injective datum.

Under AC, for an open inclusion j:U → X and its closed complement i:Z → X in a locally compact Hausdorff space, Γ_c(X,j_!A) ≅ Γ_c(U,A) and Γ_c(X,i_*B) ≅ Γ_c(Z,B), naturally and in every derived degree. Both embedding functors preserve c-softness; for compact Z the closed-piece groups identify with ordinary sheaf cohomology on Z.

Under AC on a compact Hausdorff space, the canonical refinement-limit Čech-to-sheaf comparison is an isomorphism in every nonnegative degree for every abelian sheaf, naturally and compatibly with connecting maps. Vanishing on a cofinal family of covers implies the corresponding sheaf-cohomology vanishing.

For a finite open cover of a compact Hausdorff space and given open covers of its (p + 1)-tuple intersections, p ≥ 0, there is a finite refinement with a refinement map such that each nonempty refined tuple intersection lies in one member of the corresponding prescribed tuple cover.

Under AC, an abelian sheaf E on a locally compact Hausdorff space is c-soft if H_c^1(V,E|_V) = 0 for every open V; every compact-set section then extends with compact support. Conversely c-softness implies H_c^q(V,E|_V) = 0 for every q > 0 and every open V.

Under AC, a finite compact polyhedron P of dimension d has H^q(P,F) = 0 for every abelian sheaf F and q > d, and H_c^q(U,E) = 0 for every open U ⊆ P, every abelian sheaf E on U and q > d. The same bounds hold for compact Hausdorff spaces whose every open cover admits a finite open refinement of order at most d + 1.

Under AC, let f:X → Y be continuous between locally compact Hausdorff spaces and d ≥ 0. If H_c^q(V,F) = 0 for q > d for every open subspace V of every fibre and every k-sheaf F on V, then every k-sheaf A on X admits an exact resolution 0 → A → K^0 → ⋯ → K^d → 0 whose terms restrict to c-soft sheaves on every fibre; the abelian-sheaf version also holds.

seams_checked.note: The incidence-model lemma F15 and steps 2.2 and 4.3 use the natural open-extension compact-support identity and Γ_c = Γ on the compact ambient realization. The finite deleted-boundary space is open in a compact Hausdorff polyhedron. No fixed-cover Čech comparison or c-softness of realized diagram injectives is inferred.

The operations definition and exceptional-adjoint theorem retain AC, locally compact Hausdorff bases, and the uniform bound for all sheaves on every open of every fibre. F7 explicitly limits the supplier to sheaf resolutions. Compact-section extension, support control, open/closed restriction, constant-vector tensors and acyclicity uses match the supplied results. Small direct sums are justified by a separate finite-coordinate compact-cover argument.
